text: Phosphorus deficiency (ជំងឺខ្វះសារធាតុផូស្វ័រ) as described in this source: plants show stunted, upright/narrow growth habit; few leaves, with a dark, old-green color; lower and older leaves turn a distinctive yellow-orange to reddish-purple; and tillering is poor. Recommended response: apply a balanced N-P-K basal fertilizer at planting, then topdress after the tillering stage, roughly 15 days after transplanting. Cross-reference note: this is now the third independently observed MAFF-line source describing a phosphorus-titled deficiency, after the original flagged entry (`phosphorus_deficiency_FLAGGED.json`) and a second source in Batch 9 that showed a phosphorus-heading/potassium-body mismatch (`nutrient_deficiency_phosphorus_potassium_title_mismatch_FLAGGED.json`). Unlike those two, this source's symptom description - reddish-purple/orange discoloration of lower leaves, stunted upright growth, and poor tillering - matches the classic phosphorus deficiency pattern found in general agronomic reference material, without the earlier title/body mismatch. It has not been marked FLAGGED because its own internal description is consistent, but it is worth comparing side-by-side against the two flagged entries before the open phosphorus/potassium question is formally closed, since it's possible this third source is simply a cleaner restatement of the same underlying reference material.
